hints: Look at the given $M_r$ value and compare it to the $M_r$ of simple $\text{AlCl}_3$ to work out the real molecular formula in the gas phase.
Remember aluminium chloride exists as a dimer, $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$, with two bridging chlorines that each form one normal covalent bond and one dative bond to the two aluminiums.
Count lone pairs carefully by separating the 4 terminal chlorines from the 2 bridging chlorines, since bridging chlorines use up one of their lone pairs for dative bonding.
walkthrough:
**Use $M_r$ to find the true molecule**

First, calculate $M_r$ of $\text{AlCl}_3$. That is $27 + (3 \times 35.5) = 133.5$. The gas has $M_r = 267$, which is exactly double. So the molecule is the dimer:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$$

**Picture the dimer structure**

Think of two $\text{Al}$ atoms side by side. They are joined by two bridging $\text{Cl}$ atoms in the middle, forming a central ring. Each $\text{Al}$ also has two terminal $\text{Cl}$ atoms on the outside. This is the classic electron-deficient dimer.

**Count covalent and dative bonds**

The 4 terminal $\text{Al-Cl}$ bonds are all normal covalent bonds. Each bridging $\text{Cl}$ forms one normal covalent bond to one $\text{Al}$ and one dative covalent bond to the other $\text{Al}$ using its lone pair. That gives:
$$4 + 2 = 6 \text{ covalent bonds, and } 2 \text{ dative covalent bonds}$$

**Count lone pairs on chlorine**

Each $\text{Cl}$ starts with 7 outer electrons. A terminal $\text{Cl}$ makes 1 bond, so it keeps 3 lone pairs. With 4 terminal $\text{Cl}$ atoms, that is $4 \times 3 = 12$ lone pairs. A bridging $\text{Cl}$ makes 2 bonds, one of which used up a lone pair, so it keeps only 2 lone pairs. With 2 bridging $\text{Cl}$ atoms, that is $2 \times 2 = 4$ lone pairs. Total:
$$12 + 4 = 16 \text{ lone pairs}$$

options.A: Counts the bonds correctly as 6 covalent and 2 dative, but forgets that chlorine atoms still carry lone pairs. Every chlorine has non-bonding electrons, so 0 lone pairs is impossible.
options.B: Correctly identifies the $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ dimer with 6 normal covalent bonds, 2 dative bonds from the bridging chlorines, and 16 lone pairs (12 from 4 terminal Cl plus 4 from 2 bridging Cl).
options.C: Gets the bonds right but overcounts lone pairs as 18. This is the trap of giving all 6 chlorines 3 lone pairs each, forgetting that the 2 bridging chlorines each lose one lone pair when they form the dative bond.
options.D: Describes the simple monomer $\text{AlCl}_3$ with 3 bonds and 9 lone pairs. This ignores the $M_r$ evidence that at 200 degrees C the gas is the dimer $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ with $M_r = 267$.
